# Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅga (Vb 10)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅga* is the tenth chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994]. It is devoted to the systematic analysis of the seven factors of awakening (*satta bojjhaṅgā*): mindfulness (*sati*), investigation of dhammas (*dhamma-vicaya*), energy (*viriya*), joy (*pīti*), tranquillity (*passaddhi*), concentration (*samādhi*), and equanimity (*upekkhā*) [Hazra 1994].

In standard Abhidhamma style, the chapter (PTS Vibh 227–232) organizes its material into distinct analytical frameworks. It begins with the discourse method (*suttanta-bhājaniya*), which expounds the enlightenment factors in three ways patterned on discourses in the *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (specifically SN 46:3 and SN 46:52) as well as the standard *vivekanissita* formula ("supported by seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, ripening in relinquishment") [Bodhi 2003; Ledi Sayadaw 2007]. It subsequently shifts to the Abhidhamma method (*abhidhamma-bhājaniya*), where the seven factors are analyzed strictly as supramundane path factors [Bodhi 2003]. Modern scholarship notes that the analytical portion embedded within the *Vibhaṅga* defines *bodhi-pakkhiyā dhammā* specifically as these seven awakening factors rather than as the later standard list of thirty-seven requisites [Gethin 2001]. The text is expounded in the commentary *Sammohavinodanī* (Vibh-a 310) [Bodhi 2003; Ledi Sayadaw 2007].

 DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse with other books and treatises of the Abhidhamma, most notably the *Lokuttaravipāka* of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (Ds 2.1.8) and adjacent chapters of the *Vibhaṅga* including the *Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 7) and *Maggaṅgavibhaṅga* (Vb 11), along with close textual overlap with the *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus corroborate the connection to the *Arthaviniścaya-sūtra* (D0317) and its commentary (D4365) in Tibetan, and indicate shared formulas in Śamathadeva's *Abhidharmakośopāyikā-ṭīkā* (D4094), the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99), and Ghoṣaka's *Abhidharmāmṛta* [DharmaNexus].
